vision: Redesign US cities to progressively reduce dependence on private cars while maintaining or improving equitable, practical door-to-door access through walking, bicycles, e-bikes, buses, trains and light rail.

reference_architecture.calibration: Observed data and independent detailed simulator

priorities.P0: Core MVP / first working vertical slice, with scientific prerequisites
priorities.P1: Full product beta / robustness and useful planning

epics.name: Product foundations and agent-friendly engineering
epics.outcome: Reproducible Rust-first monorepo with explicit component contracts, safe agent workflows, and architecture decisions.

stories.story: As a maintainer, I want a Rust workspace with isolated crates for ingest, graph, routing, simulation, interventions, scoring, optimization bridge, and API, so that teams can build independently.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Workspace compiles on supported Linux and macOS runners; crate boundaries and interfaces are documented.

stories.story: As a developer, I want a one-command local development setup, so that I can reproduce builds and demos.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Pinned toolchains and lockfiles; bootstrap verifies dependencies and runs a smoke test.

stories.story: As a coding agent, I want an AGENTS.md and module-specific contracts, so that I can implement features without breaking neighboring modules.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Tasks identify owned files, public APIs, tests, and prohibited cross-module changes.

stories.story: As a maintainer, I want automated formatting, linting, unit tests, and dependency checks, so that every change has a consistent quality gate.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Required CI checks are green on a clean checkout.

stories.story: As a maintainer, I want a benchmark harness with regression history, so that we catch throughput or memory regressions.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Named fixtures, hardware metadata, and comparable benchmark outputs are stored.

stories.story: As a research lead, I want versioned architecture decision records, so that technology choices remain evidence-based.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Simulator/RL/framework selections include benchmark rationale and an exit path.

epics.name: City discovery and study-area onboarding
epics.outcome: Users can locate and create repeatable transportation study areas for any supported US geography.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to search for a US city or metropolitan area, so that I can begin an analysis without GIS expertise.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Search resolves canonical geography and displays its boundary.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to choose city, metro, or drawn study-area boundaries, so that I can include commuter sheds beyond city limits.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Saved study area is a valid polygon with CRS and region metadata.

stories.story: As a planner, I want a preview of available city datasets and gaps, so that I know whether the model can be initialized.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Coverage report lists source, year, spatial extent, status, and missing required data.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to initialize a city project with a snapshot date, so that I can reproduce the starting network.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Project records boundary, source versions, baseline ID, and import status.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to expand the buffer around an urban core, so that traffic diversion outside municipal lines is represented.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Boundary change re-runs affected ingestion and clearly marks prior scenarios stale.

stories.story: As a administrator, I want batch imports of a catalog of cities, so that we can compare regional patterns at scale.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Imports are idempotent and report individual successes/failures.

epics.name: Public data connectors and provenance
epics.outcome: Ingest relevant US transportation, population, land-use and safety inputs with traceable licensing and timestamps.

stories.story: As a data engineer, I want to ingest OpenStreetMap roads, paths, turn restrictions and tags, so that the physical network is grounded in geography.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Import produces segment metadata, provenance, and a validation report.

stories.story: As a data engineer, I want to ingest GTFS transit schedules and optional GTFS-Realtime, so that existing transit routes and service frequency are represented.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Service calendars, stops, trips and transfers parse with error reports.

stories.story: As a data engineer, I want to ingest Census population and commuter origin-destination data, so that we can estimate activity locations and commute demand.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Each dataset has version, geography mapping, and known coverage limits.

stories.story: As a data engineer, I want to ingest land use and destination points, so that non-commute trips can be modeled.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Destinations are categorized and deduplicated with source traceability.

stories.story: As a data engineer, I want to integrate DOT traffic counts and observed speeds, so that the road model can be calibrated.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Observations retain location, timestamp, quality flags, and units.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want to ingest crash and emissions-related inputs, so that safety and emissions metrics use defensible evidence.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Sources and uncertainty are recorded; fatal crash and nonfatal data are not conflated.

stories.story: As a administrator, I want a licensing and freshness inventory, so that we know what data can legally be published or redistributed.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Each source records attribution, license terms, last retrieval and review state.

stories.story: As a data engineer, I want custom CSV/GeoJSON/Parquet uploads with a schema mapper, so that cities with local datasets can improve model fidelity.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Preview, schema validation and rollback work without corrupting the baseline.

epics.name: Geospatial normalization and data quality
epics.outcome: Build a consistent spatial model from heterogeneous raw sources and surface uncertainty.

stories.story: As a data engineer, I want consistent coordinates, units, time zones and identifiers, so that layers can be overlaid and joined correctly.
stories.acceptance_criteria: CRS, units, local-time handling and geometry validity are tested.

stories.story: As a simulator developer, I want snapped intersections and connected edges, so that routes do not fail due to import artifacts.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Topology tests detect dangling links, duplicate edges and impossible connections.

stories.story: As a transit modeler, I want stops aligned to reachable walking paths, so that station access times are realistic.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Unreachable stops are flagged and manual fixes are auditable.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want a per-layer completeness and uncertainty score, so that I can distinguish data absence from zero demand.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Quality dashboard shows missing regions, invalid values and confidence tiers.

stories.story: As a data engineer, I want automated anomaly reports for speeds, lane counts and connectivity, so that input errors do not become optimization results.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Outliers create reviewable findings and do not silently overwrite records.

stories.story: As a administrator, I want immutable raw inputs and derived snapshot lineage, so that a scenario can be rebuilt later.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Every derived artifact references raw hashes and processing version.

epics.name: Multimodal network representation
epics.outcome: Create a time-aware graph supporting car, walking, conventional bicycle, e-bike, bus, rail and transfers.

stories.story: As a traveler modeler, I want walking links with crossings and barriers, so that pedestrian journeys follow actual accessible routes.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Paths account for one-way access, crossings and disconnected segments.

stories.story: As a traveler modeler, I want bicycle and e-bike links with protection and safety attributes, so that mode-specific routing reflects infrastructure quality.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Routing distinguishes protected lanes, shared roads and forbidden segments.

stories.story: As a transit modeler, I want scheduled bus, train and light-rail journeys, so that transit travel includes service reality.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Edges include schedules, headways, waiting, transfers and service calendars.

stories.story: As a simulator developer, I want vehicle roads with capacity, direction and turn rules, so that driving is a valid reference mode.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Routes honor legal constraints and configurable capacity estimates.

stories.story: As a system engineer, I want stable graph serialization and version IDs, so that simulations reuse a canonical representation.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Round-trip serialization preserves connectivity and attributes.

stories.story: As a traveler modeler, I want park-and-ride and bike-on-transit/parking transfers, so that intermodal journeys are possible.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Transfer penalties, availability and restrictions are configurable.

stories.story: As a accessibility advocate, I want step-free and mobility-aid accessible paths, so that the model does not treat every traveler as able to cycle.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Accessible routing excludes impassable infrastructure and identifies unmet trips.

epics.name: Travel demand and traveler diversity
epics.outcome: Construct time-dependent trips for essential and discretionary travel while modeling heterogeneous capabilities and choices.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want time-of-day origin-destination demand for commute and non-commute trips, so that scenarios reflect the full day.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Trips have origin, destination, departure window, purpose and expansion weights.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want population-weighted synthetic travelers, so that neighborhoods are represented proportionately.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Generated totals reconcile to documented source populations within defined tolerance.

stories.story: As a traveler modeler, I want a choice set across walking, biking, e-biking, transit and car, so that mode shifts are possible after investment.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Unavailable/infeasible modes are excluded per traveler and trip.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want configurable generalized travel costs, so that choices respond to time, waiting, reliability and expense.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Parameters are explicit, unit-tested and versioned.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want trip chaining and return journeys, so that grocery and school-dropoff trips are modeled.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Multi-stop itineraries maintain realistic time windows and load constraints.

stories.story: As a accessibility advocate, I want traveler groups with different mobility constraints, so that results do not overstate bike suitability.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Groups can include noncyclists, wheelchair users, children and older adults.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want weather, season and daylight profiles, so that cycling and walking availability varies realistically.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Scenario assumptions are selectable, labeled and sensitivity-tested.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want long-term induced demand and relocation sensitivity, so that we can study adaptation over years.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Long-horizon effects are reported separately from short-term forecasts.

epics.name: Multimodal routing and door-to-door itineraries
epics.outcome: Produce realistic travel-time and flexibility comparisons across all supported modes.

stories.story: As a user, I want door-to-door routing for car and car-free modes, so that I can compare equivalent journeys.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Itinerary includes access, wait, ride, transfer, egress and arrival time.

stories.story: As a user, I want departure-time-aware transit routing, so that frequency and schedule constraints affect travel.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Off-service trips return infeasible instead of fabricated travel times.

stories.story: As a cyclist, I want bike/e-bike route selection based on infrastructure quality, so that unsafe shortcuts are not rewarded.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A tunable comfort/safety penalty is applied and inspectable.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want batch origin-destination routing, so that accessibility can be measured citywide.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Matrix jobs run deterministically against an immutable network version.

stories.story: As a user, I want multi-stop journeys and last-mile transfers, so that the model measures real errand flexibility.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Itineraries support configurable dwell times and transfer constraints.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want travel-time variability across departure windows, so that spontaneity and service gaps are visible.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Results include percentile travel times and no-service fractions.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want routing performance measurements, so that we can scale analysis sensibly.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks report paths per second, latency and memory by graph size.

epics.name: Fast transportation simulation and behavior change
epics.outcome: Evaluate infrastructure changes using a fast Rust simulator that updates mode choice, routing and congestion.

stories.story: As a simulation engineer, I want to run a deterministic baseline scenario, so that I can compare proposed networks fairly.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Same inputs and seed produce equivalent outputs with documented tolerances.

stories.story: As a simulation engineer, I want to apply network changes without rebuilding source data, so that scenario evaluation is efficient.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Simulator accepts immutable baseline plus a reversible intervention set.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want travelers to reconsider mode and route after infrastructure changes, so that removing car lanes need not assume permanent car demand.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Mode-choice iteration converges or reports nonconvergence.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want time-dependent capacity and congestion, so that road interventions model diverted car trips.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Traffic volumes and travel times respond to changes in supply and demand.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want waiting, crowding and capacity effects for transit, so that bus and rail improvements are not treated as infinite-capacity.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Boarding delay or denied boarding is modeled or explicitly bounded.

stories.story: As a simulation engineer, I want batched and parallel scenario evaluation, so that optimizers can search many alternatives.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Runs exploit multicore execution and report scenarios/second.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want sensitivity analysis over uncertain demand and behavior, so that rankings are not artifacts of a single assumption.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Multiple seeds/parameter sets yield distributions, not just a point estimate.

stories.story: As a simulation engineer, I want an abstraction layer for alternate simulators, so that engines can evolve without rewriting the product.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Same scenario schema executes through at least two adapters.

epics.name: Baseline calibration and observed-data validation
epics.outcome: Establish trustworthy historical reference conditions before making optimization claims.

stories.story: As a research lead, I want to compare modeled flows with observed traffic counts, so that we know whether road demand is credible.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Residuals and source coverage are shown by location and time.

stories.story: As a transit analyst, I want to compare modeled transit use with observed ridership where available, so that transit predictions have a reality check.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Differences are reported by route or service area with missing-data flags.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want to compare mode shares and commute times against surveys, so that baseline behavior is calibrated.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Calibration report includes targets, errors and model parameters.

stories.story: As a research lead, I want a validation holdout dataset, so that tuning does not consume all available evidence.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Held-out observations are not used for fitting and have separate scores.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want repeatable calibration runs, so that updates to demand parameters can be audited.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Calibration artifacts store seeds, source versions and parameter changes.

stories.story: As a planner, I want an explicit uncertainty/fitness banner, so that I do not mistake weak evidence for confidence.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Projects with failing calibration checks display limitations in results and exports.

epics.name: Infrastructure interventions and scenario authoring
epics.outcome: Enable valid, reversible redesign of streets, corridors, intersections, and connections.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to convert general-purpose road lanes to protected bike lanes, so that I can test reducing car-dedicated space.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Road capacity, bike connectivity and safety attributes update consistently.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to create or improve continuous pedestrian connections, so that I can test walkability changes.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Edited links connect to the pedestrian graph and obey crossing constraints.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to add or change dedicated bus lanes, so that I can test transit priority.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Road and transit travel times respond without double-counting lane capacity.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to modify a whole corridor rather than isolated segments, so that interventions provide continuous travel utility.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Tool selects connected segments and previews gaps or incompatible junctions.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to undo, redo, and version scenario changes, so that I can safely experiment.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Reverting restores the exact previous network state.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to remove or convert a road/highway segment, so that I can assess major car-capacity reductions.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Regional diversion, access continuity and emergency constraints are evaluated.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to add protected intersections and crossings, so that cycling/walking upgrades remain safe at junctions.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Intersection changes affect route comfort and crossing time.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to model land-use or destination changes separately, so that I can explore urban form as an extension.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Transport-only and transport-plus-land-use scenarios are clearly distinguished.

epics.name: Transit and intermodal service design
epics.outcome: Allow bus, BRT, tram/light rail and rail service proposals with operational realism.

stories.story: As a transit planner, I want to add or reroute bus service, so that I can serve underserved destinations.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Routes connect valid stops and have defined service calendars.

stories.story: As a transit planner, I want to change bus frequency, hours and transfer coordination, so that I can improve spontaneity and reliability.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Waiting and journey calculations update based on the new timetable.

stories.story: As a transit planner, I want to designate BRT or transit-priority corridors, so that I can test high-frequency service with dedicated capacity.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Road capacity and transit speed assumptions remain internally consistent.

stories.story: As a transit planner, I want to propose rail or light-rail lines and stations, so that I can evaluate high-capacity routes.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Routing respects stations, line frequency, travel times and transfers.

stories.story: As a transit planner, I want to add bike parking, bike access and station connections, so that intermodal journeys are practical.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Station access/egress changes affect door-to-door accessibility.

stories.story: As a transit planner, I want to estimate fleet, operator and operating requirements, so that plans are not costed as infrastructure alone.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Fleet hours and operating cost estimates accompany service changes.

stories.story: As a transit planner, I want to test timed transfers and fare policies, so that network integration can improve without new roads.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Fares, transfer timing and generalized travel costs are updated.

epics.name: Feasibility, costs, safety and physical constraints
epics.outcome: Exclude unsafe/impossible proposals and estimate implementation trade-offs with traceable assumptions.

stories.story: As a planner, I want a configurable capital and annual operating budget, so that proposals remain financially bounded.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Invalid projects are blocked and cost categories are separated.

stories.story: As a engineer, I want right-of-way and lane-width feasibility checks, so that a proposed street cross-section can physically fit.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Design violations are flagged with segment-level reasons.

stories.story: As a planner, I want emergency, disability, essential delivery and property-access constraints, so that car independence does not eliminate necessary access.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Hard constraints are tested before costly simulation.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to retain regional network connectivity for freight and essential trips, so that road reductions do not create hidden disconnections.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Connectivity tests include designated critical origin-destination pairs.

stories.story: As a engineer, I want construction, maintenance and transit operating cost models, so that lifecycle choices are comparable.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Unit-cost assumptions, year and local adjustment factors are exposed.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want collision-risk estimates separated from vehicle movement models, so that safety benefits are not invented from simulated crashes.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Risk model, exposure, calibration source and uncertainty are reported.

stories.story: As a planner, I want construction phases and disruption costs, so that the order of projects is evaluated realistically.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Each phase has a valid network and temporary-service assumptions.

stories.story: As a engineer, I want bridge, slope, utility and terrain restrictions, so that difficult locations are screened early.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Known restrictions are flagged; missing engineering evidence is labeled.

epics.name: Car independence, accessibility and equity scoring
epics.outcome: Measure the product goal directly, including all trips, populations, costs and reliability.

stories.story: As a planner, I want the share of essential destinations reachable car-free within a time budget, so that I can measure real mobility rather than lane throughput.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Scores are computed by origin, destination type, mode set and departure window.

stories.story: As a resident, I want a car-free versus car door-to-door travel-time comparison, so that I can judge practical mobility parity.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Includes walking, waiting, transfers, reliability and infeasible trips.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want an estimated car-required trip share and mode distribution, so that the main objective is explicit.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Metric definitions, assumptions and confidence intervals are published.

stories.story: As a planner, I want neighborhood-level accessibility maps, so that local improvements and gaps are visible.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Maps have population denominators and flag insufficient coverage.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to measure infrastructure space devoted to private cars, so that we can track physical car dependence.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Road-space metrics are spatially aggregated without double counting.

stories.story: As a accessibility advocate, I want equity and mobility-needs breakdowns, so that a high citywide score cannot hide isolated groups.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Results report outcomes for relevant user groups and neighborhoods.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want estimated vehicle travel and operational emissions, so that environmental outcomes remain visible.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Vehicle distance and emissions methodology are documented with uncertainty.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want a Pareto frontier of costs, accessibility, safety and car dependence, so that we can choose among non-dominated designs.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Dominance calculations use consistent constraints and units.

stories.story: As a planner, I want scenario rankings across multiple weather and service conditions, so that travel flexibility is not limited to ideal days.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Metrics include day/night, service frequency and weather sensitivity.

stories.story: As a policy analyst, I want separate short- and long-term outcomes, so that infrastructure investment is not conflated with immediate behavior.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Time horizon and behavioral assumptions are present in every score.

epics.name: RL environment and optimization specification
epics.outcome: Expose a constrained, inspectable and reproducible RL problem over sequential city redesign.

stories.story: As a RL engineer, I want a Gymnasium-compatible interface to the Rust simulator, so that learning algorithms can use a common environment.
stories.acceptance_criteria: reset/step return versioned observations, actions, rewards and terminal flags.

stories.story: As a RL engineer, I want a machine-readable action catalog and feasibility mask, so that the agent cannot choose nonexistent projects.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Invalid actions are excluded or rejected with explicit explanations.

stories.story: As a RL engineer, I want an observation encoding of network, demand, budget and accessibility, so that policies receive decision-relevant state.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Schema is documented and invariance tests detect accidental data leakage.

stories.story: As a research lead, I want a reward anchored in car independence and mobility parity, so that optimization advances the primary goal.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Weights and hard constraints are user-configurable and logged.

stories.story: As a RL engineer, I want sequential episodes with construction and operating budgets, so that ordering matters.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Each step updates cumulative network, costs and dependent metrics.

stories.story: As a RL engineer, I want batched Rust-Python bindings, so that training avoids excessive per-step overhead.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Batch APIs use bounded memory and have profiling tests.

stories.story: As a research lead, I want reward ablations and failure diagnostics, so that we detect gaming of a single metric.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Experiments log decomposed rewards, constraint failures and trivial solutions.

stories.story: As a ML engineer, I want graph-based policy observations, so that models can transfer across city topologies.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Transfer experiments compare unseen-city results with simpler representations.

epics.name: Optimization algorithms and benchmarks
epics.outcome: Find strong redesign sequences and prove whether RL outperforms simpler search.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want a random-search reference optimizer, so that we have a minimum performance baseline.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Fixed-budget runs use identical scenario evaluation and constraints.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want greedy and local-search optimizers, so that RL can be compared against practical alternatives.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Algorithms share objective scoring, compute budgets and stopping conditions.

stories.story: As a RL engineer, I want a first trainable constrained policy, so that the system can learn a sequence of projects.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint save/load and deterministic evaluation work.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want an evolutionary or multi-objective optimizer, so that we can explore trade-offs beyond one reward.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Output is a feasible non-dominated set using the same simulator.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want held-out maps and demand scenarios, so that we can test generalization.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Evaluation data and seeds are isolated from training.

stories.story: As a research lead, I want a fair comparison dashboard, so that we can assess whether RL earns its complexity.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Results include objective improvement, validity rate, compute time and variance.

stories.story: As a ML engineer, I want warm-start, curriculum or transfer training, so that policies improve across cities.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Ablations document benefit over training from scratch.

epics.name: Experiment orchestration and compute management
epics.outcome: Execute large experiments reliably, with transparent costs, reproducibility and interruptibility.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want to submit a simulation or optimization job, so that I can run work without holding the UI open.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Jobs persist with input hashes, parameters, status and result references.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want progress and partial logs, so that I can diagnose long-running experiments.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Status shows scenario count, failures and current best metrics.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want to stop and resume jobs where supported, so that compute is not wasted.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Cancellation releases resources; resumption uses compatible checkpoints.

stories.story: As a operator, I want isolated worker processes with quotas, so that one job cannot exhaust the service.
stories.acceptance_criteria: CPU, memory and concurrency limits are enforced.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want seed sweeps and parallel evaluations, so that uncertainty can be evaluated efficiently.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Artifacts identify seeds and produce an aggregate distribution.

stories.story: As a operator, I want distributed execution on multiple workers, so that metropolitan experiments can scale.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Idempotent work items retry safely and do not duplicate finalized results.

stories.story: As a operator, I want compute and storage usage reports, so that we can budget expensive runs.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Each run reports wall time, resource usage and estimated spend.

epics.name: Interactive application and spatial editing
epics.outcome: Make baseline conditions, redesign tools, and results usable in a responsive map-based web interface.

stories.story: As a planner, I want a map-based study-area wizard, so that I can select and initialize a city visually.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Boundary, dataset availability and initialization feedback are visible.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to switch among road, bike, walking, bus and rail layers, so that I can inspect the multimodal network.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Layers have legends and distinguish unknown data from absent infrastructure.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to select connected corridors and propose conversions, so that I can edit a scenario without code.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Map selection produces a preview and feasibility warnings.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to edit intervention parameters and budgets, so that I can test realistic variants.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Forms validate units and show estimated costs before applying.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to submit and follow scenario runs, so that I can connect edits to results.
stories.acceptance_criteria: UI reflects queued, running, failed and completed jobs.

stories.story: As a resident, I want before/after travel isochrones and accessibility maps, so that I can see which destinations become car-free reachable.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Maps let me choose origin, mode set, time window and metric.

stories.story: As a planner, I want linked side-by-side map and metric comparisons, so that I can inspect geographic trade-offs.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Map extents and legends stay synchronized between variants.

stories.story: As a resident, I want a responsive and keyboard-accessible interface, so that the app works across devices and needs.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Core flows have keyboard navigation, accessible labels and mobile layouts.

stories.story: As a planner, I want an animated sequence of infrastructure phases, so that I can understand how the city evolves.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Timeline shows reversible per-phase changes and related outcomes.

epics.name: Interpretation, explainability and reports
epics.outcome: Show why a design was selected and where it helps or harms residents.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to compare baseline and scenario results for core metrics, so that I can judge the effect of redesign.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Comparisons include differences, units, assumptions and uncertainty status.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to inspect effects by neighborhood, so that local regressions are visible.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Users can filter maps/tables to an area and see affected trip groups.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want to trace each optimization result to interventions, so that a result is auditable.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Every output references scenario version, projects, seeds and model version.

stories.story: As a planner, I want a step-by-step improvement chart, so that I can understand intervention order.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Each step displays incremental and cumulative metric changes.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want sensitivity and robustness comparisons, so that uncertain assumptions are not concealed.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Reports show ranges under tested demand, weather and behavior assumptions.

stories.story: As a planner, I want to view trade-offs across Pareto-optimal scenarios, so that I can select a policy preference explicitly.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Changing a priority does not silently overwrite prior scenario results.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want exportable methodology notes and known limitations, so that results are interpreted responsibly.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Report records calibration quality, causal limits and models used.

epics.name: Workspaces, APIs, sharing and export
epics.outcome: Persist projects and enable programmatic and collaborative analysis with explicit sharing controls.

stories.story: As a user, I want a saved project containing city, scenarios and results, so that I can return to my work.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Projects reopen against exact versioned inputs and show stale status.

stories.story: As a developer, I want a documented Rust API for cities, scenarios, evaluations and jobs, so that tools and agents can automate workflows.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Versioned endpoints have OpenAPI schema, validation and error contracts.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want machine-readable scenario and metric exports, so that I can reproduce analysis outside the UI.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Exports include JSON/Parquet and a versioned manifest.

stories.story: As a team member, I want workspace roles for owner, editor and viewer, so that collaboration is controlled.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Authorization tests cover read and write actions.

stories.story: As a planner, I want shareable read-only scenario links, so that colleagues can inspect results.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Public links reveal only explicitly published data.

stories.story: As a researcher, I want map and report exports, so that I can distribute results without the app.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Exports include legend, units, caveats, data attribution and date.

stories.story: As a external developer, I want a stable plugin/connector contract, so that additional datasets and optimizers can be added.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Extension manifest and compatibility tests are published.

stories.story: As a collaborator, I want project comments and review states, so that teams can discuss design trade-offs.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Comments reference a scenario revision and survive new revisions.

epics.name: Scientific verification, reliability, security and release
epics.outcome: Deliver a trustworthy, observable and maintainable public-facing system with repeatable scientific claims.

stories.story: As a tester, I want unit and property tests for graph, geometry, units and metrics, so that numeric errors are caught early.
stories.acceptance_criteria: CI includes invariants for connectivity, conservation and monotonicity where applicable.

stories.story: As a tester, I want full end-to-end tests from city import through scenario scoring, so that the core workflow actually works.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A small public fixture runs without manual steps and produces a reproducible result.

stories.story: As a research lead, I want independent detailed-simulator comparison, so that the fast engine has measured error.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Representative scenarios are cross-checked with SUMO/MATSim or a vetted equivalent.

stories.story: As a operator, I want structured logs, metrics and traces, so that failed data jobs and training runs can be diagnosed.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Each job and scenario has correlated identifiers and actionable errors.

stories.story: As a operator, I want versioned releases, migrations and backups, so that deployed results remain available.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Upgrade and restore rehearsals succeed on a staging dataset.

stories.story: As a security engineer, I want input validation, secrets management and dependency scanning, so that untrusted imports and APIs do not compromise the system.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Threat-model priorities have regression tests and secrets never enter logs.

stories.story: As a research lead, I want uncertainty and model-card documentation, so that users understand forecast limitations.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Each release documents assumptions, tested geography and failure modes.

stories.story: As a maintainer, I want Linux/macOS development and container deployment, so that developers and CI share reproducible execution.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Smoke tests pass on the supported environments.

stories.story: As a operator, I want load tests with large cities and concurrent experiments, so that performance limits are known.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Published baselines cover memory, throughput, API latency and degradation.

stories.story: As a community contributor, I want public contribution guide, licenses and sample projects, so that the platform can be adopted and improved.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A new contributor can reproduce the demo from published instructions.
